request.spec:
A period may cap the number of open claims per person (a whole number on the period form, blank
for none; PERIOD_ADDED gains cap=<n> at the end when given). Opening a claim that belongs to the
period, alone or by the bulk button, is refused with an error on the claim when the person already
has that many OPEN or PENDING claims in it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A period may cap the number of open claims per person (a whole number on the period form, blank
for none; PERIOD_ADDED gains cap=<n> at the end when given). Opening a claim that belongs to the
period, alone or by the bulk button, is refused with an error on the claim when the person already
has that many OPEN or PENDING claims in it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Periods can now have a cap on open claims per person, and opening a claim past the cap is refused. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

One thing to know: none of the tests actually hits a cap refusal. A claim belongs to the period that contains its due-by date (its own date when it has none), not the date entered on the claim. In the test, Ada's claims in early March fall outside the capped period P1, so all her opens go through. The refused bulk open in the test is refused because the claim is already open. So the refusal path itself has only been checked by reading the code, not by any test.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V80__period_cap.sql`, adds a `claim_cap` column to the period table. It is empty when a period has no cap.
- **Adding a period:** the request takes a `cap`. Blank means no cap; anything else must be a whole number of at least 1, so `0` is refused with the form's error. `PERIOD_ADDED` gets ` cap=<n>` at the end of the line only when a cap is given. Periods made by the monthly or fiscal-year generators have no cap. The as-of view of past periods also shows the cap.
- **Opening a claim:** a new check, `refuseOverCap` in `ApplyClaimStatus.java`, finds the capped period the claim belongs to. It counts that person's other OPEN or PENDING claims in the period and refuses the open if the count has reached the cap. Bulk open runs the same check and counts each refused claim. Because claims opened earlier in the same bulk run are counted, one bulk open can't push a person past the cap. The period's row is locked during the check so two users opening at the same moment can't both get past it.
- **Front end:** the period form has a `period-form-cap` field, each period row shows `period-cap`, and the period form and claim error messages now mention the cap.

Approving a PENDING claim back to OPEN isn't checked against the cap, because the request only covers opening.
